npcs.name: Aldric Venn
greet: Another one who woke in the dark. Sovereign welcomes you, Echo — the Concord asks only that you keep its peace.
Every road ends at this gate. Most of them started at the Wound.

topics.label: The tenth plinth
lines: Nine shrines stand in the Hall of Shards. Nine Echoes, nine peoples, nine prayers, all exactly the same size.
In the middle there is a tenth plinth. Empty. Our charter says only: 'leave room.' Four hundred years, and no Steward knows for whom.

topics.label: The Concord
lines: No god, no Echo and no crown rules inside these walls. That is the whole law. It is enough to keep twenty peoples from killing each other on the same street.

npcs.name: Ukka Old-Tusk
greet: Hrm. You smell like the sound.
Sit. Don't sing. Grokh don't like singing.

topics.label: What do the Grokh remember?
lines: We were there. Not our grandfathers. Us. The memory comes with the blood, whole.
The towers sang. Then the Deep Heart answered. Elves call it a tree. Kalder call it a saint. We call it what it was: a wound making noise.

topics.label: The Forest Accord
lines: Tree-elves and root-elves fought three hundred years over which end of one animal to be eaten by. We told them. They stopped. Mostly.

topics.label: Need anything, Elder?
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Lirael
greet: The Grove heals, traveller. Every season the forest reaches further.
Walk softly. The roots are listening.

topics.label: The World Tree
lines: Vael'Thorn is the wound closing. Life always closes wounds. Patience is the highest virtue — the Scream is over, whatever the Duskborn whisper.

npcs.name: Veyth
greet: ...You found me. Under the leaves, where the Sylvani do not look.
Speak quietly. Ourin is digesting.

topics.label: The Serpent
lines: The tree is not healing the wound. It is feeding on it. Everything that lives in Aurn is being eaten, slowly. We make peace with ending. They plant more trees.

topics.label: Can I help the Roots?
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Sister Maren
greet: We sing at the Grey Wall at dusk. If the singing stops, she lets go.
Hold. Hold. Hold.

topics.label: Saint Ysolde
lines: She walked into the sea and did not stop walking. She is still down there, under the harbour, one hand raised.
The Crown says she founded a kingdom. We say she is holding. Every Kalder alive is alive on borrowed stillness.

npcs.name: Old Hesk
greet: The Choir won't sing for us. The Crown won't name us. The Spire answers us, though.
Press your ear to the black tower. Go on. It never lies.

topics.label: The Still Spire
lines: Older than the ice. Older than the kingdom. Nobody built it. When you ask it something, it answers — and it has never once told us anything comforting.

topics.label: Can I ask the Spire something?
lines: I could use someone like you.

topics.label: Can I help you listen?
lines: Under the ancient cities there is a gate to a place that only listens. Go through. Tell me what it says.

npcs.name: Thrain Ledgerhand
greet: The world ended because someone asked a question. We do not ask. We feed.
Ledger's open. What do you bring?

topics.label: Kaurash
lines: The Flame Dragon is hungry. Hunger is a thing you can negotiate with. We have fed it four hundred years. Some years the ledger was short. We are ashamed of those years.

topics.label: Can I feed the dragon?
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Captain Aurelle
greet: The Throne keeps watch. The Reach will not fall a second time.
Hold, Echo.

topics.label: The word on the mountain
lines: A light came down this mountain and spoke one word to a shepherd. The word was 'Hold.' We built the city where he stood.

npcs.name: Hroald Many-Verses
greet: The world ended four hundred years ago, friend. We are living in the epilogue. Make it a good verse.
Sit by the fire. Tell me something worth singing.

topics.label: The Long Saga
lines: When the Saint walked into the sea, most of Kaldrhal knelt. We rowed. North, while the harbour was still water. The Kalder call us Oar-Breakers. We call ourselves the ones who kept the saga.

topics.label: Give me a deed to sing about
lines: I could use someone like you.

topics.label: Any raiding to do?
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Rafa al-Sahr
greet: Have you heard something that has not stopped?
The dunes still move in the shape of the old currents. Read them like water.

topics.label: The Ninth
lines: One Echo crossed our sky and never stopped. Every caravan is a pilgrimage after it. Our holy book is a map with a blank space on it.

topics.label: I will look for the Ninth
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Magister Octavia Varro
greet: The Imperium does not believe. It administrates.
Every Echo has a temple in the capital, a stipend, and a tax bill.

topics.label: The High College
lines: We have catalogued every contradiction between the nine faiths. If you lay them side by side... no. That is not a conversation for a public road.

topics.label: What are you hiding?
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Master Hoen
greet: One cut. Then the next. The sword is disposable; the cut is not.
Blossoms fall. That is the lesson.

topics.label: The Echoes
lines: The Scream was one note in a piece of music that is still playing. To build a temple to one note is to mistake a syllable for a sentence.

topics.label: Teach me
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Mayor Bramble
greet: There is enough here. There always is.
Have you eaten? You look like you haven't eaten.

topics.label: Nimtal
lines: Squat little green fellow, hands open, nothing in them. Four words of scripture: 'There is enough here.' Never hurt anybody. Never will.

topics.label: Need a hand?
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Pip Underbough
greet: Mind the cabbages!
Second breakfast is at ten, if you're stopping.

topics.label: Trouble?
lines: Goblins. In the garden. Little green nasty things, bite anything that moves, even each other. Never more than two at once, thank Nimtal.

topics.label: I can help with goblins
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Engineer Cassia Holt
greet: Echoes aren't gods. They're phenomena. Phenomena can be replicated.
Mind the steam.

topics.label: The Lattice
lines: Nine tuned towers, sunk deep, drawing power straight from the phenomenon under the world. Three are finished. The fourth breaks ground this season. The funding? Generous. Anonymous.

npcs.name: Envoy Quillon
greet: Welcome, little fragment. You are standing inside the only true word ever spoken.
Do take your fingers out of your ears.

topics.label: The Second Word
lines: Nine gods. Nine scraps of one corpse. We have heard the whole voice, every hour, for four hundred years.
The world is deaf. Deafness is the only damnation. We would only ask the question again — and let everyone hear the answer.

npcs.name: The Holy Commander
greet: The Sky Kingdom rises. When it is whole, I go down.
You came up the mountain's light. Good.

topics.label: The Sky Kingdom
lines: Aetherhold says the Silence Above never answered. It answered once. It said 'Hold.' This kingdom is built to keep saying it.

npcs.name: Ascendant Seraphine
greet: You have mud on your boots. Do not step on the glass.
The ground is where it happened. It can happen again.

topics.label: The Silence Above
lines: Our god is a silence — a sound that left and never landed. We pray upward into nothing, and nothing answers. That is how we know it is clean.

topics.label: How do I earn your trust?
lines: I could use someone like you.

topics.label: Let me prove myself above
lines: The Valkyries test every groundling who climbs this high. Most fall. Fall gracefully.

npcs.name: Nhal
greet: Shh. Listen. ...There. Did you hear it come back?
We were thrown. The others were unmade. We landed past the edge.

topics.label: The Far Side
lines: The Scream reached the edge of the world and found nothing to echo off. We build towers of crystal to catch the last of it as it comes back from the void.

topics.label: How can I help you listen?
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Sebastian
greet: The Vigil is closed to the living. You, however, are not exactly living, are you?
His Majesty does not receive. I do.

topics.label: The King
lines: His Majesty has no name. A name is the first thing the Lightbringer asks you to give up. He kept three guards and gave up everything else.

npcs.name: Ser Ysolde
greet: Do not ask about my name.
I hold this hall. I do not leave it.

topics.label: Your name
lines: ...Everyone asks. My mother named me for the statue in the square. She did not know what the statue is. I do.

npcs.name: Archmage Ysmer
greet: Spells are only sounds that learned manners.
Ink, paper, patience. And a great deal of essence.

topics.label: What is spellcraft?
lines: Every school of magic is a register of the Scream, tamed. Fire is Kaurash's register. Ice is Ysolde's. Holy... well. Whose is holy, would you say?

topics.label: Teach me spellcraft
lines: I could use someone like you.

topics.label: Are there darker books?
lines: There are books written under the sea, in the deeplings' ink. I would like to read one. From a distance.

npcs.name: Morvhal
greet: Everything has a price. I just write it down.
Sign here. And here. Don't read that part.

topics.label: What is a pact?
lines: The dead are only quiet, not gone. A pact asks them to stand up for you. They always say yes. The question is what they ask afterwards.

topics.label: I want to make a pact
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Ilsabeth
greet: Every living thing leaves a spirit when it dies. Most people step on them.
Mind the wisps.

topics.label: Spirits?
lines: Arcane, sacred, wicked, eldritch... a creature's spirit is the shape the Scream left in it. Weave enough of them and steel remembers being alive.

topics.label: Teach me to see spirits
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Sensei Raiden
greet: Steel and spell are one stroke.
Breathe. Cut. Speak the word. Cut again.

topics.label: The Storm Spell school
lines: We are the only sect that casts while we cut. The Petal Court thinks it impure. The Petal Court has never fought a storm.

topics.label: Teach me the Storm Spell
lines: I could use someone like you.

npcs.name: Old Saelis
greet: Dragons are not Echoes. They are older. The Scream only made them angrier.
Mind your eyebrows.

topics.label: What are dragons?
lines: Fire, ice, storm — three bloods, one beast. They were here before the Aurnathi dug their towers. When the Scream came, the dragons were the only things that screamed back.
A dragon bonds with the first face it sees when it hatches. Not the bravest. Not the kindest. The nearest. Remember that.

topics.label: Teach me to raise a dragon
lines: I could use someone like you.

Sovereign City has work for anyone willing.

topics.label: About Sovereign City

topics.label: Do you need supplies?
lines: Sovereign City is short of paper for the embassies. Bring me 24 and the town will remember it.

topics.label: Is anything threatening you?
lines: We lose people to bandits on the Sovereign roads. Deal with 8 of them and come back to me.

topics.label: Anything to deliver?
lines: Our letters to the Arcanum keep going missing on the road. Carry this one by hand.

topics.label: What does the city need most?
lines: The Oathbreaker of the Concord walks near Sovereign City. And the stores are low on glass for the Hall of Shards. Both, if you can.

topics.label: Do you need supplies?
lines: the Nether's Heart is short of blaze rods for the chorus-fires. Bring me 8 and the town will remember it.

topics.label: Is anything threatening you?
lines: We lose people to the wailing things that drown out the Word. Deal with 6 of them and come back to me.

topics.label: Anything to deliver?
lines: Our letters to the Brimstone Citadel keep going missing on the road. Carry this one by hand.

topics.label: What does the city need most?
lines: The Warped Choir walks near the Nether's Heart. And the stores are low on quartz for the resonators. Both, if you can.

npcs.name: Ishvane
greet: Welcome to the Cinder City, traveller.
the Cinder City has work for anyone willing.

topics.label: About the Cinder City
lines: the Cinder City? Inside the Word. You hear it too, a little. Everyone does, here.

topics.label: Do you need supplies?
lines: the Cinder City is short of quartz for the resonators. Bring me 24 and the town will remember it.

topics.label: Is anything threatening you?
lines: We lose people to wither skeletons in the deep halls. Deal with 5 of them and come back to me.

topics.label: Anything to deliver?
lines: Our letters to the Nether's Heart keep going missing on the road. Carry this one by hand.

topics.label: What does the city need most?
lines: The Warped Choir walks near the Cinder City. And the stores are low on blaze rods for the chorus-fires. Both, if you can.

npcs.name: Valen
greet: Welcome to the Sky Kingdom, traveller.
the Sky Kingdom has work for anyone willing.

topics.label: About the Sky Kingdom
lines: the Sky Kingdom? The Sky Kingdom of the Throne. Built to keep saying 'Hold.'

topics.label: Do you need supplies?
lines: the Sky Kingdom is short of ambrosium for the beacons. Bring me 16 and the town will remember it.

topics.label: Is anything threatening you?
lines: We lose people to storm-creatures on the sky-roads. Deal with 8 of them and come back to me.

topics.label: Anything to deliver?
lines: Our letters to Aetherhold keep going missing on the road. Carry this one by hand.

topics.label: What does the city need most?
lines: The Thunderhead walks near the Sky Kingdom. And the stores are low on zanite for the bells. Both, if you can.

npcs.name: Altair
greet: Welcome to Aetherhold, traveller.
Aetherhold has work for anyone willing.

topics.label: About Aetherhold
lines: Aetherhold? Aetherhold. Do not touch the glass with mud on your boots.

topics.label: Do you need supplies?
lines: Aetherhold is short of golden amber for the windows. Bring me 12 and the town will remember it.

topics.label: Is anything threatening you?
lines: We lose people to pests on the outer isles. Deal with 8 of them and come back to me.

topics.label: Anything to deliver?
lines: Our letters to the Sky Kingdom keep going missing on the road. Carry this one by hand.

npcs.name: Quorr
greet: Welcome to the Brimstone Citadel, traveller.
the Brimstone Citadel has work for anyone willing.

topics.label: About the Brimstone Citadel
lines: the Brimstone Citadel? Inside the Word. You hear it too, a little. Everyone does, here.

topics.label: Do you need supplies?
lines: the Brimstone Citadel is short of blaze rods for the chorus-fires. Bring me 8 and the town will remember it.

topics.label: Is anything threatening you?
lines: We lose people to the wailing things that drown out the Word. Deal with 6 of them and come back to me.

topics.label: Anything to deliver?
lines: Our letters to the Nether's Heart keep going missing on the road. Carry this one by hand.

topics.label: What does the city need most?
lines: The Warped Choir walks near the Brimstone Citadel. And the stores are low on quartz for the resonators. Both, if you can.

npcs.name: Vesh
greet: Welcome to Castle Blackhall, traveller.
Castle Blackhall has work for anyone willing.

topics.label: About Castle Blackhall
lines: Castle Blackhall? The Far Side. We listen for the sound coming back from the void.

topics.label: Do you need supplies?
lines: Castle Blackhall is short of pearls to tune the crystals. Bring me 8 and the town will remember it.

topics.label: Is anything threatening you?
lines: We lose people to shulkers clogging the spires. Deal with 4 of them and come back to me.

topics.label: What does the city need most?
lines: The Chorusent walks near Castle Blackhall. And the stores are low on chorus fruit for the towers. Both, if you can.

npcs.name: Thessaly
greet: Welcome to the Arcanum, traveller.
the Arcanum has work for anyone willing.

topics.label: About the Arcanum
lines: the Arcanum? The Arcanum. Neutral ground, like Sovereign: every school of magic is taught here, and no god is prayed to. Spells are only sounds that learned manners.

topics.label: Do you need supplies?
lines: the Arcanum is short of amethyst for the resonance halls. Bring me 16 and the town will remember it.

topics.label: Is anything threatening you?
lines: We lose people to renegade spellcasters near the castle. Deal with 8 of them and come back to me.

topics.label: Anything to deliver?
lines: Our letters to the Desert Town keep going missing on the road. Carry this one by hand.

topics.label: What does the city need most?
lines: The Renegade Magus walks near the Arcanum. And the stores are low on books for the library. Both, if you can.

npcs.name: Sylvaine Thorne
greet: A spell is a sentence. Most people only know nouns.
Mind the starbuncle. He steals.

topics.label: What is a glyph?
lines: A word the World Tree taught us before the Scream. Write enough of them in a row and the world does what you wrote. The Arcanum says it is crude. The Arcanum has never grown a forest in an afternoon.

topics.label: Teach me glyph-magic
lines: Glyph-magic runs on Source - the life of growing things, gathered. Bring me amethyst and I will bind your first book.

npcs.name: Brakka Deepdelve
greet: There are worlds under the world. Not the deep dark. Older. Stranger.
Bring a torch. Bring three.

topics.label: Worlds under the world?
lines: Caves full of magnets. Caves full of bones that still walk on their own legs. A sea under the mountain with things in it that pray. Mount Kharuun dug past them all and pretended not to see.

topics.label: What is under the mountain?
lines: Down there are caves that should not exist. Go and see one. Bring back proof.

npcs.name: Captain Elric Vane
greet: The Watch does not sleep. Neither do the things outside.
Stay off the roads after dark, Echo.

topics.label: What comes at night?
lines: Since the Wound opened wider, things crawl out after dusk that were never alive in the first place. Pumpkins with men inside. Hounds made of bad dreams. The further north-east, the worse.

topics.label: I can stand watch
lines: The Watch needs blades that come back from the dead. You'll do.

npcs.name: Mother Orsa
greet: Every old song has a beast in it. Most of the beasts are real.
Sit. Have soup. Then I'll tell you what's eating the sheep.

topics.label: Which beasts?
lines: Basilisks in the dry hills. Gargoyles that wake on church roofs. Armour that walks without a knight in it. And the great ones: the Kraken, the Sandworm, the Yeti of the north. My grandmother sang about all of them. She was right about all of them.

topics.label: Which beasts are real?
lines: All of them. Go and meet a few. Come back and tell me which verse they were in.

quests.title: A Sound Still Travelling
quests.intro: You woke in the sculk, whole and nameless. Every road in the Reach leads to Sovereign, the Free City. Start there.

stages.text: Reach Sovereign, the Free City
lines: Gold and purple roofs. Twenty peoples on one street. Nobody looks surprised to see you.

stages.text: Speak with the Steward at the Citadel
lines: You are the second Echo through my gate this week. Or the first, twice — with your kind it is hard to say.
The Grokh say they know what you are. Nobody believes the Grokh. Go and ask them anyway. And see the Archmage before you go — you will need more than a sword.

quests.title: What the Grokh Remember
quests.intro: The Grokh camp lies on the dry side of the Elven Wilds, far to the north-west. They worship nothing — and they say they know why.

stages.text: Find Ukka Old-Tusk in the Grokh camp
lines: Hrm. Two of you. Loose bits of the sound, walking around in bodies.
Before I talk, you work. Goblins in the dry grass. Dust of a dead Echo. Kill them; they're only the twitch of something already gone.

stages.text: Kill goblins on the orc side of the Wilds
Return to Ukka
lines: Good. Now listen, because I say this once.
You are fragments of the One Scream that never found a people. That's why you come back when you die. A sound doesn't stay dead. It repeats.
One of you leans to the dark behind things. One of you leans to the light above things. Both of you are the same noise. Remember that when they make you hate each other.

quests.title: Two Echoes
quests.intro: Ukka sends you on — each to the ones who will claim you. Go together; the road is long.

stages.text: Ask Ukka where to go
lines: The dark one: the Vampire Isle, far south-east. The Vigil spares your kind. The bright one: the Holy City, on the mountain island in the south sea. The light came down there.
Go to both. Together. The ones who claim you will both try to make you choose.

quests.title: The Vigil Opens its Gate
quests.intro: The Vampire Isle. The Vigil spares a Shadow Lord on sight — and nobody else.

stages.text: Cross to the Vampire Isle (far south-east)
lines: Black cliffs, a castle with every window lit, and no sound at all.

stages.text: Speak with Sebastian, the Royal Butler
lines: A Shadow Lord. His Majesty felt you arrive. Your companion may wait at the gate — I will see that nothing eats them.
The Fallen Order burns our kind on sight. Their Seraph, Ashveil, holds the Ashen Wastes south of Sovereign. Bring the Vigil his silence.

stages.text: Slay Ashveil, the Fallen Seraph, in the Ashen Wastes
Seek out Ser Ysolde in the castle halls
lines: Ashveil is ash. Then you may hear it. The statue in our square — the Lightbringer with her spear in a dragon's skull.

There was no dragon. It was added a hundred and forty years later. The statue is a woman frozen with one hand raised. Go and see the Saint under Kaldrhal's harbour. Then tell me they are not the same woman.

reward.message: The Vigil will remember your face. The Corrupted Blade is yours.

quests.title: The Envoy from Below
quests.intro: Something in the Nether wants to meet you. Its envoys are always polite. Take the great Fantasy Portal north of Sovereign (x -352, z -904); in the Nether, go east.

stages.text: Reach the great portal north of Sovereign
lines: A gate of black stone and basalt, taller than a tower. Behind the purple sheet, the air hums.

stages.text: Find the Nether's Heart (Nether, east of the arrival)
lines: Inside the Wound, the sound never stopped. The walls hum.

stages.text: Meet Envoy Quillon
lines: A Shadow Lord. Do you hear it in your shades? A little of the whole voice. You are halfway home already.
Join us. Or prove you are not ours: our Apostle walks the Heart. Silence it, and we will understand each other perfectly.

stages.text: Slay the Apostle of the Undivided in the Nether's Heart
Return to Quillon
lines: Refused, then. Politely. I respect that. We will ask again. We are very patient, and you, little fragment, do not die.

quests.title: The Word on the Mountain
quests.intro: The Holy City stands where the light came down, on the mountain island in the south sea. Its knights hunt every dark thing — your companion included. Talk fast.

stages.text: Reach the Holy City on the Mountain island
lines: White walls round a portal of glowstone. The bells ring once when you arrive.

stages.text: Speak with Captain Aurelle
lines: Divinity. The Throne knew you would come. Your shadowed friend stays outside the walls — the Knights cannot help what they are.
A shepherd of ours fell to the dark and walks the mountain in his armour. Give him rest.

stages.text: Give the Fallen Shepherd rest (Holy City)
Return to Captain Aurelle
lines: Rest, brother. ...Now go north, to Kaldrhal. Find the Choir of the Still Water. They sing a word at their wall every dusk. Tell me which word.

reward.message: The Throne gives you the Divine Punisher.

quests.title: Hold
quests.intro: The Choir of Still Water sings at the Grey Wall of Kaldrhal, the Ice Kingdom, in the east.

stages.text: Find Sister Maren of the Choir in Kaldrhal
lines: The word? We sing 'Hold.' It is what she is doing, under the ice. Holding.
Bring us harbour-glass for the beads — the blue kind — and you may stand a night with us.

stages.text: Bring Sister Maren 8 prismarine shards (harbour-glass)
lines: Bead by bead. Hold, Echo.

stages.text: Ascend to the Aether (the Holy City portal) and find the Sky Kingdom
lines: A city of a thousand towers, floating. Bells, and no wind.

stages.text: Stand before the Holy Commander
lines: 'Hold.' The Choir sings it. We sing it. The Saint said it, under the water.
Two faiths, a sea apart, one word. When they hear each other, both will change. You will be there when they do.

quests.title: The Quiet Edge
quests.intro: Both roads lead to the frozen harbour of Kaldrhal, and the sword nobody may draw.

stages.text: Find Old Hesk in the Ashfoot quarter of Kaldrhal
lines: Two of you. The Spire said two would come. It said one would be dark and one would be bright, and that it would not matter.
Under the harbour there is a sword. The Quiet Edge. Four silences to draw it: empty hands, three tokens freely given, the eye of the Wide Mouth, and not one word.
Something guards the ice for the King. Go and see what he keeps.

stages.text: Destroy the King's Ice-Warden at the Royaume d'Alstom
Ask the Choir what drawing the sword would mean
lines: If the sword is drawn, the splinter leaves the wound. The ice thaws. The Wide Mouth wakes. Please. Not yet.

quests.title: The Forest Accord
quests.intro: Back to the far north-west: the Accord in the Wilds holds by a thread, and something walks there that is neither elf nor orc.

stages.text: Carry the Grokh message to Lirael of the High Bough
lines: A message from the orcs? ...'The tree and the serpent are one animal.' They say it every year. Every year we pretend not to hear.
Take seedlings to the root-folk. A gift. Let them see we can give without taking.

stages.text: Bring Lirael 8 oak saplings for the gift
lines: These will grow in the dark if they must.

stages.text: Find Veyth, hidden under the canopy, and give the gift
lines: Saplings. From the canopy-folk. ...The Roots will plant them. Under the tree. Where it eats.
Tell her also: something old woke in the south of the Wilds. A colossus of roots. It is looking for something.

stages.text: Fell the Rootbound Colossus in the southern Wilds

quests.title: The Far Side
quests.intro: The Endlings listen at the edge of the world. Find the End — and Castle Blackhall out past the void.

stages.text: Slay the Ender Dragon that guards the way
Reach Castle Blackhall in the End (east of the main island, past the void)
lines: Dark towers over nothing. Purple light. Very far away, a sound, coming back.

stages.text: Find Nhal, the Last Listener
lines: You came. Shh. Listen... There. It came back changed. Someone on the surface is building towers that sing.
Nine of them. Find out who. But first — the Guardian in the castle undercroft has stopped listening and started eating.

stages.text: Destroy the Guardian of the Far Side (Blackhall)
summon: The Guardian of the Far Side

quests.title: The Lattice
quests.intro: Aldergear, the Cogwright city far in the north-east, builds tuned towers sunk deep. Somebody pays for them.

stages.text: Ask Engineer Cassia Holt about the Lattice in Aldergear
lines: The Lattice? Three towers done, fourth breaking ground. Power from the phenomenon under the world. Revolutionary.
Funding? Anonymous. The schematics too — old ones, from under the ground. And the fourth tower has... a guardian now. Nobody built it.

stages.text: Destroy the Lattice Engine at Aldergear
Tell Cassia who pays for the Lattice
lines: Malgorath. The Screamborn. We are building them a mouth. I'll bring it to the Compact. They'll file it as a complaint. They always do.

quests.title: The Storm Above
quests.intro: Up through the Holy City portal: the Sky Kingdom is under siege by a storm with a will.

stages.text: Reach the Sky Kingdom in the Aether
lines: The bells are ringing out of time. The clouds are moving against the wind.

stages.text: Bring down Cumulonimbus over the Sky Kingdom
Report to Ascendant Seraphine in Aetherhold
lines: The storm was the Silence trying to speak again. Groundlings stopped it. Do not expect thanks. ...Thank you.

quests.title: Inside the Word
quests.intro: Down into the Nether: the Heart's furnaces are feeding the Lattice. Put them out.

stages.text: Put out Ignis in the Nether's Heart
Break the Forge of the Second Word in the Cinder City (Nether, west)
summon: The Forge of the Second Word

stages.text: Kill the Wither of the Wound (Cinder City)

quests.title: The Hollow Bell
quests.intro: Far west, Isar-Thal holds a copy of the Scream in a bell. Something is circling it.

stages.text: Dive to Atlantis (Isar-Thal), in the far western sea
lines: Domes of black glass. A sound under the sound, like a heart.

stages.text: Kill the Leviathan circling the Hollow Bell (stay in the water)
Kill Scylla, the pirates' sea-witch, at Pirate Port

quests.title: The Glass Province
quests.intro: South, in the Nasiri desert: the drowned Thalassi city under the dunes is waking.

stages.text: Ask Rafa al-Sahr about the glass under the dunes (Egyos Enemus Yar)
lines: A city under the sand? ...We walk over it. The dunes move like water there. Something stood up out of them last night.

stages.text: Destroy the Remnant risen from the Glass Sea
summon: The Remnant of the Glass Province

quests.title: The Wound
quests.intro: The far north-east. The Ruins of Aurn, where the Abyssal Cult preaches the Second Word over the oldest wound in the world.

stages.text: Reach the Ruins of Aurn (far north-east)
lines: Black stone, sculk in the cracks, and a choir that never stops.

stages.text: Slay Vael, the Hollow Prophet
Silence Maledictus at the Spire
summon: Maledictus, Voice of the Second Word

stages.text: Destroy the Withered Choir

quests.title: The Echo Below
quests.intro: Under the Ruins, the last Listening Spire goes down into the Deep Dark — and through it, into the echo of the world.

stages.text: Descend the Spire of Aurn (deep, under the Ruins)
lines: The sculk breathes. The Wardens turn their blind faces toward you — the citizens of Aurnath, listening.

stages.text: Cross into the Otherside, the echo of the world (Deeper Darker portal)
lines: Everything here is an echo. Including you.

stages.text: Slay the Wardens of the echo (3)
Destroy the Deep Heart's Echo

reward.message: The echo is silent. The weapons of the end of the world are yours.

quests.title: Leave Room
quests.intro: Every story starts at the Citadel gate. This one ends there too — for now.

stages.text: Return to the Steward in Sovereign
lines: You have been everywhere. You have heard every people tell the same story wrong. Sit.
The tenth plinth. I think I know who it is for now. Not a god. A listener — someone who will one day stand before the Deep Heart and decide whether to ask it again.
Two of you came through my gate. One dark, one bright, the same noise. Whatever you decide, decide it together. The Reach is listening.

reward.message: Book II of the Sundered Reach is told. Book III begins at the Citadel gate.

quests.title: The Short Year
quests.intro: North of Sovereign, the Emberkin feed a dragon that is getting bigger than its mountain. Their ledger is short this year.

stages.text: Find Thrain Ledgerhand in the Dwarf Kingdom
lines: The Everfed is hungry, and the ledger is short. In a short year we feed it... other things. The old. The volunteers.
Unless someone fills the ledger. Gold. And something is eating in the lower shafts that isn't Kaurash.

stages.text: Bring Thrain 16 gold ingots for the ledger
lines: Entered. Sixteen. No one goes down the shaft this year. ...Thank you.

stages.text: Kill the thing eating in the lower shafts of the Dwarf Kingdom
summon: The Thing in the Lower Shafts

stages.text: Return to Thrain
lines: It was eating the offerings before they reached the dragon. That is why Kaurash grew hungrier. Not bigger. Hungrier.
Write that down, Echo. Every faith in this world is feeding something — and something else is always eating on the way.

quests.title: The Oar-Breakers' Cargo
quests.intro: Far north, over the sea: the Skjald-folk rowed away the day the harbour froze. Ysolde's hand points north. At them.

stages.text: Find Hroald Many-Verses at the Viking Fjord
lines: The Saint's hand? Aye, it points at us. Our oldest verse says so. Our oldest verse also says what we took in the boats.
Her sword-hand's twin. A splinter of the same ice. We buried it on the Isle, under the barrow. And the dead in the barrow have stopped sleeping.

stages.text: Lay the Barrow-King of Viking Isle to rest
Return to the skald
lines: The barrow is quiet. And the splinter? Still there. Cold as the day we took it. It hums when you two stand near it. Both of you.
That is a verse I did not expect to sing. The Saint did not point at us. She pointed at whoever would come for this. Two noises, one sound.

quests.title: There Is Enough Here
quests.intro: South, in the farmlands: the smallest god in Aurn is the only one getting stronger. Nobody has noticed. Go and notice.

stages.text: Visit Mayor Bramble in the Villager Capital
lines: Trouble? No trouble. There's never trouble here. Have you eaten?
Well — the Imperium sent tax-men again. They found nothing worth taking. They never do. Help with the harvest, would you?

stages.text: Bring Mayor Bramble 64 wheat for the harvest feast
lines: Look at that. Enough. There's always enough.

stages.text: Join the harvest feast at the Hobbit Village (Pip Underbough)
lines: Second breakfast, third breakfast, feast! Sit! ...You two have been everywhere, haven't you? Gods and dragons and the ends of the world.
Here, nobody's fighting about what the Scream meant. We just say: there is enough here. And there is. Funny how that works.

reward.message: Nimtal grows a little stronger. Nobody notices. That is the point.

quests.title: The Blossom-Fall Ronin
quests.intro: South-west, in the mountains of Sazane: the sects are the only people who call the Quiet Edge heresy. They want to meet the two Echoes everyone is talking about.

stages.text: Find Master Hoen of the Huashan Sect
lines: So. The two noises. The Court has a question for you: if you found the Quiet Edge, would you draw it?
Do not answer. Answer with your blades. A ronin of ours went to the Emei sect to steal its last blossom. He brought the dead with him.

stages.text: Defeat the Blossom-Fall Ronin at the Emei Sect
Return to Master Hoen
lines: You cut like two people who have stopped arguing. Good.
Remember this: a blade that ends things forever is the only true heresy. Everything else should be allowed to fall, like blossoms. Even you.

quests.title: The Licence of Gods
quests.intro: The Imperium licenses all nine gods and believes in none. Its High College has a secret, and a Sentinel guarding it.

stages.text: Find Magister Octavia Varro in Ancient Egypt
lines: You two have heard every faith tell the same story wrong. So have we. We wrote it all down. Nine Echoes, one event.
The Censor's legion of possessed armour hunts anyone who reads it. And the Sentinel of the Nine Temples guards the original.

stages.text: Destroy the Censor's possessed legion (anywhere)
Defeat the Sentinel at the Great Monument of Egypt
summon: The Sentinel of the Nine Temples

stages.text: Return to Magister Varro
lines: The original thesis. Nine Echoes, one wound. If this is published, every temple in the Imperium loses its legal basis.
Keep a copy. Both of you. One day the world will need to hear it, and it will need to hear it from someone it cannot tax.

quests.title: Break the Lattice
quests.intro: Varro's thesis, Nhal's warning, Cassia's 'anonymous' money: now you know what the towers are. Three are finished. Each sings through a Lattice Heart at its foot. Break them before the fourth is done.

stages.text: Meet Engineer Cassia Holt in secret in Aldergear
lines: You're back. Good. The Compact filed my report as a complaint, just like I said.

Each finished tower sings through a Heart at its foot — a tuned shard of something from under the world. Break the Hearts and the Lattice goes deaf. The Compact Wardens will come. Then run, and don't stop.

stages.text: Break the first Lattice Heart (west tower)
Break the second Lattice Heart (south tower)
Break the third Lattice Heart (east tower)
Escape Aldergear before the Compact catches you
lines: Behind you the three towers fall silent, one after another. Somewhere far below the world, something that was about to speak... does not.

stages.text: Tell Ukka Old-Tusk at the Grokh camp
lines: Hrm. The towers stopped singing. We heard it from here. Four hundred years we told them. You two did it in one night.
They will build again. Mouths always want to talk. But not tonight.

reward.message: The Lattice is deaf. The Book of Aurn has a new page.

quests.title: The Second Word
quests.intro: The tenth plinth is still empty. But someone has started asking the Deep Heart's question again - and it is not you.

stages.text: Speak with the Steward in Sovereign
lines: Envoys of Malgorath came to the embassies last night. Polite. Patient. They asked every crown the same thing: who will speak the Second Word?
A hall of the Word was found in Aetherhold's clean sky and cast down into the Nether. It is called the Brimstone Citadel now. Go and see who lives there.

stages.text: Reach the Brimstone Citadel in the Nether (around 1537, 97, 14)
lines: Black stone and brimstone, built to the roof of the world. Every wall hums the same note.

stages.text: Break the Citadel's guard (12 of its fire-bound)

quests.title: The Cantor-Prime
quests.intro: The Citadel's Cantor-Prime keeps something in its heart that answers when you speak.

stages.text: Defeat the Brimstone Colossus that wakes in the Citadel's heart
Tell the Steward what the Citadel was building
lines: A choir. A machine that sings. Built to carry one word a very long way.
Aldergear's Lattice towers are the same shape. Someone has been paying for both.

quests.title: The Silence Above
quests.intro: Ascendant Seraphine sent word down: the sky over Aetherhold has started to thunder in words.

stages.text: Go up to Ascendant Seraphine in the third Sky Castle (Aether, around 4240, 302, 6776)
lines: Groundling. The Silence Above has never spoken except once. Now the storm over us repeats a single word, over and over.
Kill the storm. Do not listen to it.

stages.text: Defeat the Thunder That Speaks over the Sky Castles

quests.title: The Listening Deep
quests.intro: Old Hesk says the Spire under Kaldrhal has stopped answering questions and started asking them.

stages.text: Speak with Old Hesk in Kaldrhal
lines: The deep dark listens. Always has. But below it there is another place - the Otherside, the miners call it - where the listening has teeth.
Something there heard the Second Word and wants to repeat it. Go down. Make it quiet.

stages.text: Silence a Stalker of the Otherside (Deeper Darker)
Clear 10 of its listeners

quests.title: The Under-Wonders
quests.intro: The Under-Delver of Mount Kharuun found a sea under the mountain where something prays the Second Word.

stages.text: Speak with Brakka Deepdelve in the Dwarf Kingdom
lines: Past the magnet caves, past the bone-walkers, there is a drowned dark. The Deep Ones there pray. The prayer is one word long.
And there are bigger things. Things that were old when the dragons were young. Kill one of the great ones and the praying stops for a while.

stages.text: Bring down one of the great ones of the caves (Tremorzilla, Luxtructosaurus or the Hullbreaker)

quests.title: The Night of the Wound
quests.intro: Every night more horrors crawl out of the Ruins of Aurn. Captain Vane of the Night Watch has a plan, and it is a bad one.

stages.text: Speak with Captain Elric Vane of the Night Watch in Sovereign
lines: The things that come at night have lords. Headless, pumpkin-crowned, laughing. Kill the lords and the rest scatter.
They hold court at the Ruins of Aurn, far north-east. Go at night. Bring friends.

stages.text: Defeat the Headless Lord at the Ruins of Aurn
summon: The Headless Lord of the Wound

quests.title: The Lattice Engine
quests.intro: Engineer Cassia found what the Lattice towers were for. She is frightened, and she was never frightened before.

stages.text: Speak with Engineer Cassia Holt in Aldergear
lines: The towers are a throat. Four towers, one voice, powered from below. When the engine wakes, it will say the Second Word for all of us.
The engine is already awake. It built itself a body.

stages.text: Destroy the Lattice Engine under Aldergear

quests.title: Hold
quests.intro: The towers are silent. The Citadel is broken. The envoys are gone. For now.

stages.text: Return to the Steward in Sovereign
lines: Silence. Real silence. I had forgotten what it sounds like.
They will try again. Malgorath is patient, and the Deep Heart is still down there, waiting to be asked.
But the Reach has two Echoes now that chose to keep it whole. That is a new word. Not the second one. Ours.

reward.message: Book III of the Sundered Reach is told. The Reach goes on.

quests.title: Enough Bread

stages.text: Bring Mayor Bramble 16 bread for the festival
lines: Enough! There's always enough. Thank you, dear.

quests.title: Goblins in the Garden

stages.text: Kill 5 goblins
Tell Pip the garden is safe
lines: Oh, wonderful! Cabbages saved! Have a pie. Have two.

quests.title: The Short Ledger

stages.text: Bring Thrain 12 gold ingots for the ledger
lines: Entered. Your name — well, your noise — is in the book now. The Everfed thanks you.

quests.title: A Verse Worth Singing

stages.text: Kill 6 Bloodfang Reavers in the Frozen Marches
Return to the skald
lines: Six Reavers! That's a verse. 'And the loose noise came north, and the Reavers learned silence.' Not bad. Not bad.

quests.title: Raid the Black Flag

stages.text: Kill 8 pirates at Pirate Port or Pirate Cove (west sea)
Tell the skald of the raid
lines: Ha! The Black Flag sells dead Thalassi to the Collector. Good riddance.

quests.title: Something That Has Not Stopped

stages.text: Go to the Ruins of Aurn, the Wound, far north-east, and listen
lines: Under the wind there is a sound that does not stop. It is not the Ninth. But it is listening back.

stages.text: Tell Rafa what you heard
lines: Not the Ninth... but something heard you. Write it in the margin of the map. Every margin matters.

quests.title: The Suppressed Thesis

stages.text: Bring Magister Varro 6 books to copy the forbidden thesis
lines: Six copies. One for each road out of the capital. If they burn the College, the idea survives. ...Nine Echoes, one event. There. I said it.

quests.title: One Way to Cut

stages.text: Cut down 10 bandits on the roads
Return to Master Hoen
lines: Ten cuts. None the same. Good. The blade is disposable. You are learning that you are not.

quests.title: What Eats in the Dark

stages.text: Kill 10 spiders in the dark hollows
Return to Veyth
lines: The spiders took our young. You took them. The Roots will not forget a stranger who goes into the dark for us.

quests.title: The Wailing Stone

stages.text: Bring Ukka 10 amethyst shards (they hum)
lines: Hrm. Hums. Same as the sound, quieter. We bury them. Nobody should sell this to Aldergear.

quests.title: Ask the Spire

stages.text: Go to the Still Spire's quarter at the far side of Kaldrhal and listen
lines: You press your ear to the cold stone. It answers a question you did not ask: "You are what they tried to make."

stages.text: Tell Old Hesk what the Spire said
lines: ...It told you that? Then the King's Vault is closer to done than we thought.

quests.title: Clean Hands

stages.text: Clear 8 Aether pests from the sky-roads
Return to Ascendant Seraphine
lines: Acceptable. For a groundling. You may walk on the outer glass.

quests.title: Catch the Echo

stages.text: Silence 10 endermen (they interrupt the listening)
Return to Nhal
lines: Quiet. Thank you. ...Now I can hear it. It says your names. Both. As one sound.

quests.title: The Scribes' Order I: Ink and Paper

stages.text: Bring the Archmage 16 lapis lazuli
lines: Good. Lapis remembers the sky. Here — your first book, and the table to write in it.

quests.intro: The Arcanum — the Magic Castle south-west of Sovereign — is neutral ground for every school of magic. Its Archmage teaches spellcraft to anyone who will listen.

quests.title: The Scribes' Order II: Stolen Pages

stages.text: Take back stolen spell pages from witches and evokers
Return the pages to the Archmage
lines: Evokers write in blood, you know. Messy. But the spells are real. Your book can hold more now.

quests.title: The Scribes' Order III: The Arcane Anvil

stages.text: Bring 16 amethyst shards to tune the anvil

stages.text: Defeat the Dead King, who comes for the Archmage's codex (at the Arcanum)

quests.title: The Scribes' Order IV: The Ancient Codex

stages.text: Defeat two great Cataclysm beings anywhere in the worlds
Return to the Archmage
lines: Two of the great ones, and you still have both hands. The Codex is yours. Read it slowly.

quests.title: The First Contract

stages.text: Gather the souls of 15 restless dead
Bring the souls to Morvhal

quests.title: The Dark Scroll

stages.text: Bring Morvhal 4 ghast tears (ink for the scroll)
lines: Tears of the Wound. Perfect ink. Sign — there.

stages.text: Collect the debts of 10 illagers and witches

quests.title: The Great Pact

stages.text: Defeat the Debt-Collector that came for Morvhal's ledger
Return to Morvhal
lines: It came for my ledger and found you. The Great Pact, then: a staff that commands what you killed.

stages.text: Present your work to Archmage Ysmer at the Arcanum (the Magic Castle, south-west of Sovereign)
lines: So the pacts answer to you now. The Arcanum records it: one more school mastered by a loose Echo.
Every school of magic is a register of the Scream, tamed. You are collecting registers. Be careful what they add up to.

stages.text: Cut down 10 bandits with steel and spell

quests.title: Armour of the Storm

quests.title: The Wyrm-Speaker

stages.text: Bring Old Saelis 32 cooked beef (a hatchling eats more than you)
lines: Good. You can feed something. That is the first half of it.
The second half: a dragon respects only what it could not kill. Come with me.

quests.title: Cinderjaw

stages.text: Defeat Cinderjaw, the wild drake of the Mountain Castle
Return to Old Saelis
lines: Cinderjaw yields. Now each of you must find your own. One of you is dark — your dragon is out in the storm. One of you is bright — yours sleeps in the ice.
Beat the mother, take the egg, and be the first face it sees.

quests.title: The Black Storm
quests.intro: The Lightbringer is the part of the Scream that refused to stop. Its dragon is a storm that never ends — a black lightning wyrm over the Vampire Isle.

stages.text: Defeat Ashcloud the Unbound in the storm over the Vampire Isle
Bring word to Old Saelis
lines: Ashcloud. Black storm-blood. Her egg is yours. Hatch it in the rain — lightning dragons wake to thunder. Be the face it sees.

reward.message: A black lightning dragon egg. Place it out in the rain and stay close when it hatches.

quests.title: The White Choir-Wyrm
quests.intro: Ysolde's Echo is stillness. Its dragon is a white ice wyrm that sleeps under the harbour of Kaldrhal and sings with the Choir.

stages.text: Defeat Hymnfrost, the Choir-Wyrm, by the Royaume d'Alstom
Bring word to Old Saelis
lines: Hymnfrost. White ice-blood — the Saint's own colour. Her egg is yours. Hatch it underwater: ice dragons wake in the cold. Be the face it sees.

reward.message: A white ice dragon egg. Place it under water and stay close when it hatches.

lore.title: The One Scream
lore.text: Four hundred years ago there was one people, the Aurnathi, and one world. They built their cities down instead of up, and nine Listening Spires to hear the Deep Heart beneath the stone. They asked it its name. It answered once. Nobody agrees what the answer meant. Everyone agrees on when: the ice remembers it, the desert is made of it, the deep cities are still full of it.

lore.title: The Nine Echoes
lore.text: The Scream split as it travelled, and each fragment became something: a saint in the ice, a dragon under a mountain, a tree, a serpent, a small green god, a light that would not stop, a silence above, a note that fell to earth, and a ninth that never stopped moving. Every people found one. Every people built a faith on it.

lore.title: Sovereign and the Concord
lore.text: After the war nobody won, every crown agreed on one patch of ground nobody would own. Sovereign, the Free City: twenty peoples, one street, and the Concord — no god, no Echo and no crown rules inside its walls. In the Hall of Shards nine shrines stand, all the same size. And a tenth plinth, empty. The charter says only: leave room.

lore.title: Kaldrhal and the Saintess
lore.text: When the Scream came north on the back of a kraken, a woman walked into the sea and did not stop walking. The harbour froze from the horizon inward. Saint Ysolde is still down there, one hand raised. The Crown says she founded a kingdom. The Choir says she is holding. The Ashfoot do not worship her at all: they listen to a black tower nobody built.

lore.title: Mount Kharuun
lore.text: The dwarves were the deep-miners, too far down to be unmade. Heat fell inward when the world cracked and woke a dragon, Kaurash, the Everfed. The Emberkin do not pray. They feed. Their holiest book is a ledger.

lore.title: Greenhollow
lore.text: The farm-folk got the smallest Echo: Nimtal, a squat green figure with open, empty hands. Four words of scripture: There is enough here. Greenhollow has never started a war. Everyone else finds this adorable or intolerable.

lore.title: Vael'Thorn and the Root-Halls
lore.text: Where the wound tried to close, something enormous grew. The Sylvani in its shade saw a World Tree and call it healing. The Duskborn in the caves beneath saw something coiled and swallowing, and named it Ourin, the Serpent. They have fought three hundred years over the right word for a plant.

lore.title: The Grokh
lore.text: The orcs live in the same forest as both elf nations and worship nothing. Everyone calls it stupidity. The Grokh do not build towers, do not write, and do not sing — and when asked why, they only say: we were there.

lore.title: The Vigil of Vaelmoor
lore.text: Kalder once — the ones who asked why the Saint got to decide that everyone stops. Exiled, they crossed to a dark island and worship the Lightbringer, the part of the Scream that refused to end. They do not die; that is the whole theology. A nameless King, a butler who opens every gate, ten knights, and a statue of a woman with a spear in a dragon's skull.

lore.title: The Silent Throne and the Umbral Court
lore.text: Two kinds of loose Echo walk the Reach now. The Divinity of the Holy City, where a light came down the mountain and said one word to a shepherd: Hold. And the Shadow Lords, who take up the Monarch's blades and raise what they kill as shades. The Vigil spares the second. The first hunts it.

lore.title: Aetherhold
lore.text: Some of the Scream went up and never came back. The Unfallen live on floating stone and never touch the ground, where it happened. Their god is an absence; they pray upward and nothing answers. They consider that proof it is clean.

lore.title: Malgorath, the Wound
lore.text: The Nether is not another realm. It is the inside of the Scream, still happening. The Screamborn were pulled through it. They worship the whole sound, not a fragment, and believe the world is deaf. They want to make it hear again: the Second Word. Their envoys are always polite.

lore.title: The Far Side
lore.text: Where the Scream reached the edge of the world and found nothing to echo off. The Endlings were thrown, not unmade, and landed beyond the edge. They build crystal towers to catch the last of the sound coming back from the void.

lore.title: Aldergear
lore.text: Imperial engineers and Emberkin exiles who decided the Echoes are phenomena, not gods, and phenomena can be replicated. Cold-engines that mimic the Saint, furnaces that mimic the Dragon. And the Lattice: nine tuned towers, sunk deep, drawing power from beneath the world.

lore.title: Isar-Thal
lore.text: Under the western sea the Thalassi kept the Scream — the sea does not let a sound stop. In the Hollow Bell they listen to it still. They need no god. They have the recording.

lore.title: The Skjald-Holds
lore.text: When the Saint walked into the sea, most of Kaldrhal knelt. Some rowed north while the harbour was still water. The Kalder call them Oar-Breakers. They keep the Long Saga: the world ended four hundred years ago, and the only holy thing left is to be worth singing about.

lore.title: The Petal Court
lore.text: Sazane arrived late, from across the eastern water, and found every people worshipping a single note. They found it embarrassing. The Court venerates impermanence; its sects guard the mountains, and call a blade that ends things forever the only true heresy.

lore.title: The Glass Sea
lore.text: The desert was ocean. When the Scream crossed it, the water stopped. The Nasiri descend from the fleets that sailed it, and every caravan is a pilgrimage after the Ninth Echo, the one that never stopped. Their holy book is a map with a blank space.

lore.title: The Twin-Crown Imperium
lore.text: The river-kings and the legion-cities merged on one doctrine: do not pick a god, take them all. Every Echo has a licensed temple and a tax bill. The largest army in Aurn, and a High College that knows more than it publishes.

lore.title: Sunken Aurnath
lore.text: Beneath the Ruins of Aurn lie the buried cities. Sculk to the ceilings. Wardens in every hall — not monsters but the citizens, blind and deathless, still listening. At the deepest point, the Deep Heart. It has not spoken since.

lore.title: What You Are
lore.text: Ukka Old-Tusk said it plainly. You are fragments of the One Scream that never found a people — loose Echo-matter in a body. That is why death does not hold you. A sound does not stay dead. It repeats. One of you leans to the dark behind things, one to the light above them. Both of you are the same noise.

lore.title: The Grokh Were There
lore.text: The Grokh are not a people who came after. They are Aurnathi survivors, the burden-bearers who stood too far from the Spires to be unmade. They remember the Scream as a memory, not a story, passed whole in the blood. That is why they will not build towers or sing.

lore.title: The Statue Is the Saint
lore.text: Ser Ysolde of the Vigil told it: the Lightbringer's statue had no dragon until the third Court added one. It is a woman frozen with one hand raised. Kaldrhal and Vaelmoor worship the same woman — one calls her the saint who stopped, the other the light that refused to stop.

lore.title: Hold
lore.text: The Holy City's light said one word: Hold. The Choir of Still Water sings the same word at the Grey Wall. It is what the Saint said under the water. Two faiths, a sea apart, one word.

lore.title: The Quiet Edge
lore.text: Under Kaldrhal's harbour a sword of black glass stands in warm water: Ysoldskarn, the Quiet Edge, the only blade that can wound an Echo. Four silences to draw it: empty hands, three tokens freely given, an eye of the frozen kraken, and not one word. Drawing it thaws the ice. The kraken wakes. The Thalassi will help you. Ask yourself why.

lore.title: One Animal
lore.text: The tree and the serpent are one being. The Sylvani see the part that reaches; the Duskborn see the part that eats. The Grokh told both for three hundred years. You carried the saplings that started the Forest Accord.

lore.title: Something Always Eats on the Way
lore.text: Kaurash was not growing bigger. Something in the lower shafts was eating the offerings before they reached it, so it grew hungrier. Every faith in Aurn is feeding something, and something else is always eating on the way.

lore.title: Who Pays for the Lattice
lore.text: Cassia Holt traced the anonymous money and the old schematics. Malgorath. The Screamborn are funding Aldergear's towers. The engineers think they are building a power grid. They are building a mouth — nine towers, the way the Aurnathi built nine.

lore.title: The Saint's Other Hand
lore.text: The Oar-Breakers took a splinter of Ysolde's ice north in the long-boats and buried it under a barrow. It hums when the two of you stand near it. The Saint did not point at the skalds. She pointed at whoever would come for it.

lore.title: Nimtal Is Winning
lore.text: Of all nine Echoes only the smallest is growing stronger, because it is the only one worshipped by people who are content. The other eight are fed by fear. Long-term, Nimtal wins. Nobody has noticed. That is very much in character.

lore.title: Nine Echoes, One Event
lore.text: The High College proved it and buried it: all nine Echoes are one event, heard from different distances. Every temple the Imperium taxes rests on not saying so. You carry a copy.

lore.title: The Lattice Went Deaf
lore.text: You broke the three Hearts and ran. The towers fell silent. Something far below that was about to speak did not. Aldergear will build again — mouths always want to talk — but the doomsday clock went back.

lore.title: The Second Word
lore.text: Malgorath's whole design: someone on the surface, in the dark, asking the Deep Heart the question again — willingly. Their envoys keep asking you. You keep refusing. They are patient, and you do not die.

lore.title: The Deep Heart's Echo
lore.text: Under the last Spire, in the echo of the world, the Deep Heart's own echo stood up to stop you, and the First Listener with it. You silenced it. The Heart itself still waits below Sunken Aurnath — finished, or waiting to be asked again.

lore.title: The Tenth Plinth
lore.text: The Steward believes it now: the empty plinth in the Hall of Shards is for a listener — someone who will one day stand before the Deep Heart and decide whether to ask it again. Two of you came through the gate. Whatever you decide, decide it together.
